slides.title: Faraday Future Launches FF Nexus Academy Summer Camps
slides.highlight: Faraday Future is implementing immersive summer camps for students to advance an embodied AI robotics education strategy, which aligns with RwB's focus on embodied learning.

slides.title: Simulating human-robot decision making for embodied AI
slides.highlight: This work explores simulating human-robot decision making, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Towards Agentic Agent-based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
slides.tldr: INTEGRATING LLM-BASED AGENTS INTO ABM SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores replacing symbolic rules in agent-based models with LLM-driven decisions, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Investigates the feasibility and impact of replacing symbolic ABM rules with LLM-based agentic tool-calling capabilities.
card.key_idea: Extends the Schelling segregation model in Mesa by delegating one agent's neighbor classification to a local LLM (Qwen3.5) using tool calls to update similarity counters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using robustness checks (M1-M4) and Statistical Model Checking via MultiVeStA. Results show larger LLMs are reliable but introduce significant runtime overhead.
card.limitation: Small LLMs exhibit operational fragility, semantic errors, and tool-call failures, potentially compromising simulation reliability.

slides.title: On the Structure of Address in Multi-Party Dialogue: From Discrete Labels to Continuous Levels
slides.tldr: CONTINUOUS ADDRESSEE MODELING IN MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This research explores addressee detection as a continuous phenomenon rather than discrete labels, analyzing its relationship with listener behaviors like gaze and backchannels. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Addressee detection in multi-party dialogue is better modeled as a continuous level than discrete labels.
card.key_idea: A latent-variable model transforms categorical annotator labels into continuous address levels, representing addressivity as a graded property rather than a multi-class classification task.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the Teidan corpus (Japanese triads) using Bayesian mixed-effects models. Continuous levels showed better predictive fit (ELPD) for turn-taking, gaze, and backchannels.
card.limitation: Limited to Japanese triadic discussions; address levels were inferred from only three categorical annotations per turn.

slides.title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC PERSONA ADAPTATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored, psychologically grounded personas through user interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PACE enables humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored personas through interactive user Q&A and multimodal embodiment.
card.key_idea: An interactive elicitation pipeline uses adaptive Q&A to generate a structured, psychologically grounded PersonaSpec, which is then mapped to the Ameca robot's dialogue and facial expressions.
card.evaluation: Tested with 25 participants using BFI-44, economic games, and Likert scales; PACE significantly outperformed static baselines in psychometric alignment and perceived interaction quality.
card.limitation: Relies on cloud-based inference and ASR, potentially introducing latency and transcription errors in noisy environments.

slides.title: S.E.A.G.R: A Socially and Emotionally Aware Greeting Robot Framework with Dual-Layer Cultural and Affective Modulation
slides.tldr: CULTURALLY AND EMOTIONALLY ADAPTIVE GREETING FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: This framework introduces a dual-layer modulation system for greeting robots that adapts based on cultural identity and affective cues, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A robotic greeting framework that adapts gesture type by culture and execution by user emotion.
card.key_idea: A dual-layer Sense–Think–Act architecture using badge-based cultural mapping for greeting selection and facial expression analysis to modulate gesture amplitude, duration, and vocal tone.
card.evaluation: Implemented as a low-cost proof-of-concept prototype using Arduino and Python; no empirical user studies were conducted.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation through user studies and relies on badge-scanning, which does not generalize to open public spaces.

slides.title: How Reliable Are Multimodal Signals of Conversational State? Evidence from Remote Dyadic Collaborative Tasks
slides.tldr: EVALUATING MULTIMODAL SIGNALS FOR CONVERSATIONAL STATE
slides.highlight: This work evaluates the reliability of linguistic, acoustic, and interaction features for predicting cognitive load and power roles, which informs HyECHO's goals for robust multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Multimodal signals of conversational state often lack generalizability and reliability once speaker identity is controlled.
card.key_idea: A three-dimensional framework (predictive accuracy, cross-task generalizability, and test-retest reliability) evaluated interactional, acoustic, and linguistic features using the AVCAffe dataset of remote dyadic collaboration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 53 dyads across 9 tasks using LODO cross-validation, LOCO analysis, and ICC. Results show linguistic features predict best but generalize poorly.
card.limitation: Conversational power prediction remained near chance, likely due to task-level aggregation and the structural constraints of dyadic interactions.

slides.title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO
slides.tldr: HUMAN ARM GESTURE IMITATION FOR SEMI-HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a system for a semi-humanoid robot to imitate human arm gestures using a pose-estimation model and analytical geometry, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A system for the NICO robot to imitate human arm gestures using monocular RGB input.
card.key_idea: Uses MediaPipe for 3D landmark extraction and analytical geometry to compute joint angles, which are then linearly mapped to NICO's specific motor configurations.
card.evaluation: Tested with six participants across 11 poses and three viewing angles. Results show moderate accuracy for most joints, with MAEs between 10° and 34°.
card.limitation: High reconstruction error for forearm rotation (50.1° MAE) and sensitivity to self-occlusions and complex poses.

slides.title: Modeling turn-taking with distant viewing: investigating silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse
slides.tldr: SILENCE THRESHOLDS IN HUMAN AND AI DISCOURSE
slides.highlight: This study analyzes silence gaps in human and AI-generated audiovisual material, contributing to the understanding of turn-taking and engagement for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Study compares silence thresholds in human sitcoms versus AI-generated synthetic podcasts.
card.key_idea: Analysis of silence gaps across speaker gender and production settings using fundamental-frequency thresholds estimated via Praat.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 30 US situational comedies and 51 Google NotebookLM synthetic podcasts; results based on gap comparisons.
